- **Strengths:** Fast point location and neighbor finding without explicit parent pointers; simplified logic compared to Frisken and Perry [5] [S1].

The evidence explicitly supports all aspects of the claim. It confirms that point location and neighbor finding are performed without floating-point arithmetic (by casting to integers), which implies speed. It states that the method omits parent pointers from the node structure to minimize footprint, relying instead on a parent_trace array and traversal stack. Finally, it explicitly contrasts the method with Frisken and Perry [5], noting that it omits the distinction of whether a neighbor is 'left' or 'right' on midplanes, thereby simplifying the logic.

It differs from Frisken and Perry by omitting the distinction of "left" or "right" midplane neighbors and by precomputing bit-depth shifts to avoid expensive arbitrary left-shifts [S1].

The claim states that the method differs from Frisken and Perry by omitting the distinction of 'left' or 'right' midplane neighbors and by precomputing bit-depth shifts to avoid expensive arbitrary left-shifts. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms both points: 1) Under 'Neighbor Finding', it states 'Frisken and Perry [5] require foreknowledge of whether the neighbor is “left” or “right” on each X,Y,Z midplane. As our traversal only neighbor-finds when necessary, we omit this distinction...'. 2) Under 'Point Location', it states 'repeatedly left-shifting bits by arbitrary integers is expensive. Thus, we precompute child_bit_depth[d]... and left-shift by 1 or 2...'. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
